sources.summary: Government news item (发布日期 2026-09-23 10:20; PubDate meta 2026-09-23 10:20) by the New Area planning and construction bureau, the authority that handles construction completion filings. It states that the second-batch construction works of the Huawei Cloud Horinger Data Center project - Yungu West Zone (Phase 1) have recently completed their completion-acceptance filing (竣工验收备案), a key step towards production and operation. The second batch has 45,717.7 m2 of floor area and comprises the 2# data-centre machine-room building and the 2# generator (oil-engine) platform, planned to put close to 4,000 cabinets into production, enough for nearly 20,000 servers. Operation is described as a future step.
sources.date_semantics: Published 23 September 2026. Read as a government observation that construction of the second-batch works (2# machine-room building and 2# generator platform) was complete, with completion acceptance filed, on or shortly before the publication date; 'recently' (近日) gives no exact filing day, so the publication date is used. Operation, cabinet counts and server numbers are planned figures and are not asserted.

sources.summary: EIA report form (94 pages; compiled September 2024 by an environmental consultancy for Huawei Cloud Computing Technology Co., Ltd., 华为云计算技术有限公司) for the indoor 220 kV substation (3 x 100 MVA initially, 8 x 100 MVA planned; one two-storey station building 147.1 m x 42.2 m, 6,310.59 m2) of the Huawei Cloud Horinger Data Center project - Yungu West Zone (Phase 1). It locates the project in the Yungu area of Horinger New Area east of Jingu Road, south of Yunzhan Avenue, west of Shengguo Road and north of Yunchi Avenue, prints the station centre as E111°48'10.292", N40°32'0.593", and says the Bank of China data centre lies 144 m west and the Agricultural Bank of China data centre (under construction) to the north. It states that the substation is one of the buildings of the West Zone Phase 1 project, built entirely inside that project's land, and that the project's main works had already started (main works need no EIA under a 2024 Hohhot EEB reply; only the substation needed one). Appended filing notice (Horinger New Area Management Committee, 13 June 2024, project code 2306-150123-89-04-325368) lists the West Zone Phase 1 scope: about 174,096 m2 of land, about 151,831 m2 of floor area, three data-centre machine-room buildings with generator platforms and buried oil tanks, a power control workshop, a chemical store, one 220 kV substation and a gatehouse, planned 2023/07-2027/03. Printed monitoring points on the four sides of the station and a Bank of China data-centre noise point are given in tables 3-8 and 3-10.
sources.date_semantics: Published with the approval-result publicity of 10 February 2025; report compiled September 2024, PDF created 10 January 2025. Used for the locator, campus identity and owner; it is outside the status window and its construction statements describe 2024.
sources.coordinate_crs: Geographic degrees-minutes-seconds printed without a stated datum or accuracy; transcribed arithmetically to decimal degrees with no datum transformation. The four printed side points are internally consistent with the centre and the building dimensions, and independent Esri WGS84 imagery shows the station building at the printed position; the GCJ-02 alternative contradicts the imagery (see the geometry facts file).

sources.summary: Government news item (发布日期 2026-10-12 11:31; PubDate meta 2026-10-12 11:31) on a waste-heat cooling project in which the China Mobile Hohhot Data Center (中国移动呼和浩特数据中心) and Inner Mongolia Jingneng Shengle Thermal Power use a 4.6 km existing heating pipeline to turn power-plant waste heat into chilled water for data-centre cooling. It states that the China Mobile Hohhot Data Center's B02 machine building has been put into operation (B02机楼已投运), with its PUE reduced from 1.315 to 1.209 and about 560,000 kWh saved so far, and that further savings are expected once all machine buildings are built and connected. It names no other building, gives no capacity and does not say when B02 first entered service.
sources.date_semantics: Published 12 October 2026. Read as a present-tense government statement that the B02 machine building was operating (running IT load with a measured PUE) on the publication date. The original service date of B02, the cooling project's commissioning date and the PUE measurement period are not stated and are not asserted.

sources.summary: EIA report form (59 pages; PDF created February 2023) for two indoor 110 kV substations ('Data 1#' and 'Data 2#', each 2 x 63 MVA) of the Agricultural Bank of China Data Centre Third Branch Horinger New Area construction project (项目代码 2106-150123-89-01-134187), invested and built by the Agricultural Bank of China Inner Mongolia Branch. It locates the project on plot E01-04-01 at the south-west end of the Yungu area of Horinger New Area, prints the two station centres (Data 1#: 111°48'16.892", 40°32'15.910"; Data 2#: 111°48'37.714", 40°32'22.320") without a datum, and says both stations are inside the data-centre campus on its south side, either side of the south main gate, about 20 m north of Yungu Heng 44 Road. It describes the campus: Phase 1 with 6 machine-room buildings, 4 power buildings, 2 spare-parts stores, an office building, 2 substations and gatehouses, planned to enter production in 2024; Phase 2 with 14 machine-room buildings planned for 2030; total load about 366 MW. Its figure 4 site plan draws one rectangular campus about 1,159 m by 391 m with the Phase 1 core in the middle and the two substations on its south side.
sources.date_semantics: Published with the approval-result publicity of 15 March 2023. Used for the locator, campus identity and owner; it is outside the status window, and its production years are forecasts.
sources.coordinate_crs: Geographic degrees-minutes-seconds printed without a stated datum or accuracy. Comparison of the report's own site plan with independent Esri imagery shows the values are in the GCJ-02 web-map offset frame; the selected point was converted to WGS84 (compiled coordinate transform; see the geometry facts file).
